_note: Macrotermes (M7). Used by termites so far: nest (with the foraging holes), queen_body, founding, mound (with how often a walk may use a chimney), food (what they gather, when they go out: at night and in the rain; find_radius: how near a worker must come to a plant to find it, the colony only goes for plants its workers have found and told of; no bread; the pieces are built into fungus comb in the garden rooms; regrowth: eaten dry grass grows back green from its roots after ticks, and a tuft eaten within bare_radius blocks of a foraging hole leaves the grass block under it bare, coarse dirt, until then), garden (the garden rooms and how fast the fungus nodules grow, how the comb ages: a fresh layer ripens after about ripen_ticks, a ripe layer goes old when a nodule grows from it or after about old_ticks, an old layer nobody eats crumbles after about crumble_ticks, and the Termitomyces mushrooms that come up after rain round a colony with a healthy garden), laying (the queen's steady stream of eggs; queen meal = how many nodules she holds), the nurses, and from brood max_young, hatch_ticks, larva_meal (nodules a nymph eats) and larva_starve_ticks, and colony max_workers; soldiers (how many the colony wants per worker, minors to a major, the nodules a nymph eats to grow into a minor or a major, how often a soldier wants a nodule from a nurse, how far apart the minors stand along the foragers' trail, and how long at most they wait outside for the workers to come in when the foraging is over); alarm (how long each alarm level lasts after the last thing that raised it: 1 footsteps, 2 an enemy at the foragers, 3 a break-in, 4 repeated break-ins; how many break-ins within how long make level 4; how many more soldiers the colony wants after a level 4 and for how long; how far a soldier feels another's drumming). The queen's rich meal, burst and incubation are not used by termites; her starve_ticks is: the queen, and the king by her rule, die after that long wanting food and getting none (the king wants a nodule every worker meal_interval_ticks), here or while away, but only once the colony has had its first comb (hungry_from_first_food). worker: the workers eat once every meal_interval_ticks, slow down after slow_after_ticks without a meal and starve after starve_after_ticks; worker.diet (real Macrotermes): the young (nurse age) eat fungus nodules (nurse_food), the older ones old comb (store: a layer of comb over its bed), either eats the other kind when its own is not there, one piece makes workers_per_piece meals, and the hunger clocks only start once the colony has had its first comb (hungry_from_first_food); mouth_to_mouth: the nurses eat the nodules and feed the queen, king, soldiers and nymphs mouth to mouth from their crop, head to head, instead of carrying the nodule in their jaws; the worker ages (nurse_until_ticks, builder_until_ticks) are, for jobs by age. nest.new_holes (the user's decision): when the colony knows a rich plant (rich: true) more than min_distance blocks from every hole, the workers dig a tunnel underground to it and open a new hole beside it, plugged for good once the food is gone; the tunnels reach from reach_min blocks out (young colony) to reach_max (at reach_full_at_workers workers), the foragers range as far; at most max new holes at a time. nest.crust_walls (the user's decision, 2026-10-14): the gallery walls are thin mud crusts, plastered over every side that would open to the outside before the termites dig through it ("wall first"); a whole missing block (a player broke in) is still packed full with plug_block. nest.sheeting (mud sheeting): rich food near a hole (nearer than new_holes.min_distance) gets a covered runway of mud crust over the ground from the hole to it, at most max_length blocks long, eaten from under it by day too; at most max runways at a time; a runway crumbles once its food is gone. refuse: termites have no refuse chamber; a body younger than eat_fresh_ticks is carried into a garden and eaten (one layer of comb), an older one is walled up with soil where it lies; one nobody gets to crumbles after corpse_decay_ticks. colony (the brain, part 1): max_workers is the most workers the colony can grow to (most of them are numbers inside the nest); real_cap the most real mobs while a player is within watch_radius blocks of the nest; crew how many real workers keep working while nobody is near (the same as real_cap: the user wants a loaded colony to work just as before whether a player is near or not; lower it to save server work); swaps_per_second how many come out of the numbers or go back in each second (only where no player can see).
_parts_note: The colony parts this species has besides the ones every colony has (Project Apex, colony parts step 2; the names are signed up in colony/ColonyParts.java, a name nothing signed up stops the game loading with a message). Every colony has: nest, nest_walls, food_store, food_map, queen_care, brood, refuse, foraging_holes, foraging_trails, danger_map, neighbours, population, away_life, nest_ledger, nest_life, field_life, build_life, worker_food. Macrotermes adds king care (a royal pair), the mound, closed holes, hidden trips through the galleries, the fungus garden, Termitomyces mushrooms, soldiers and the alarm.

neighbours._note: Brain step 4g, step 5 (the user's answers of 2026-10-18; real neighbouring Macrotermes wall off their galleries where they come close): workers on the surface meet as the ants do, and a gallery piece coming within 'within' blocks of another Macrotermes colony's gallery is a meeting for both. The colony yields as the ants do (young_meetings at founding down to 1 at old_at_days): its tip there stops, a piece grown that way is not dug, and a piece whose tip it yields at is walled off (wall_galleries: packed with soil back to its fork, out of sight, nobody inside; the 4 arms only stop). The webs never join (a piece touching the other gallery is never dug). My picks as for the ants, to confirm.

danger._note_close: Brain step 4g, step 3 (real Macrotermes after a raid): close_holes plugs at once every foraging hole within reach blocks of where a termite was hurt or killed (not only a hostile seen), and every hole whose gallery out from the nest runs that near it; they stay shut, get no turn, draw no growing tip and no food is fetched there until the danger fades below dangerous_from. A place once as strong as leave_from (two deaths, or a death and a hurt) and attacked at least twice (attacks less than seen_every_ticks apart are one; each termite counts once an attack, at its worst; BUGS 65) is left for good: its holes within merge_within are never opened again, and a new hole is opened on the same gallery at least new_hole_from blocks from it. My picks, to confirm.

lost._note_lost: Brain step 4g, step 4 (the user's decisions, 2026-10-18): a number's trip near remembered danger can be lost out of sight, per_point for each point of danger, at most most; in loaded land only while a hostile is really there, in unloaded land the memory decides. A lost member counts in the memory as a death only if nestmates find the body: certain within found_within blocks of the nest, found_drop_per_block less likely each block farther. My picks, to confirm.

trails._note: The foragers' trail memory (brain step 4a): each way out the foragers use gets a trail toward the food they found, 1 stronger per visit (at most most_strength); unused, its strength halves every half_life_ticks and below fade_below it is forgotten. No trunk: Macrotermes forage under cover, through their tunnels and holes, not on bare open paths. My picks, to confirm.

galleries._note: Termites underground (docs/plans/termites-underground.md), the switch: enabled false brings back the 2 holes of before, both open every foraging time. Step 1, holes take turns: the tunnels reach out in 4 arms arm_length blocks from the middle; holes about hole_spacing blocks apart along every tunnel; each foraging time 1 hole open per foragers_per_hole foragers (at least 1), rain_more times as many again in the rain; holes with known food within food_radius blocks open first, explore of them (none if only 1 opens, 1 if 2 or 3) go to the holes rested longest (with no known food, all do). Step 2a, galleries grow tip by tip: the galleries in all may be workers / workers_per_block blocks long, at most max_length (the arms are the least; a giant colony would otherwise fill the whole circle), no tip farther than reach blocks from the middle; the shortest tip grows first by piece_length blocks, wandering up to wander degrees and away from the other tips; a tip forks in two (fork_angle degrees either side) after fork_min to fork_max blocks of growth. Step 2b, hidden trips: a termite whose route runs at least hidden_trip blocks along a closed stretch of gallery leaves the world and comes out at the far end after the walk's time; if anything breaks in on the way, everyone travelling there shows up where they would be by then (0 = off, all walk). Step 3, growing toward food (the user's decisions, 2026-10-17): rich food the colony knows far from every hole gets a gallery piece dug straight to it from the nearest dug gallery (it may lie as far out as reach); known grass within pull_reach blocks past a tip pulls that tip toward it; only then do the tips spread evenly. A tip stops at its food while it lasts. A far piece that has led to no food for fill_days game days (counted while away too) is packed with soil, from the far end back to its fork, once nobody is in it and no player can see it; the 4 arms never fill in. Its length may only be dug again toward food. My picks, to confirm.

wood_call._note: Big dead wood calls the galleries (the user's pick, 2026-10-19; real termites smell rotting wood and its fungi through the soil, and feel how big a log is from how it vibrates): dead wood of at least min_blocks blocks together (a standing dead giant, a fallen giant) is noticed from reach blocks past any dug hole or growing tip, from big_reach once it is big_blocks blocks or more; the colony then knows its foot, and a gallery piece (or a runway, from a hole near it) goes to it before the tips spread evenly. A big find gets the diggers (the user's pick, 2026-10-19): the way to such wood may take the galleries up to over_limit blocks past the length the workers allow; the even spreading waits until the workers catch up. reach 0 = off. My numbers, to confirm.

body_language._note: How the bodies behave (the animation engine, 2026-10-16; every number my pick, to confirm). No naps or hot ground for termites yet. notice: Macrotermes workers are blind and feel the ground shake: a player walking within range blocks, or sprinting, jumping or landing within shake_range, makes an idle worker freeze with its antennae raised for look_ticks (from, to), with chance; it never turns to look. Then it does not freeze again for rest_ticks.

fight._note: M8 step 2a, the shared fight system (fight.FightNumbers). Health and damage per body, the same numbers the bodies had in code before (nothing changes in-game). stings_to_fall: how many Matabele stings paralyse it (M8 step 2b, my picks, to confirm): a worker or minor 1, a major soldier 2 (the biggest, its head armoured), king and queen 3 (never reached: raids hit feeding spots, never the mound). foe_types: chickens peck termites (step 6c). foe_species: the Matabele, the termites' real enemy, fought wherever it comes from. venom_ticks (M8 fight polish, round A; my picks, to confirm: the speed of Megaponera venom on termites is not measured in the papers): after the felling sting the termite staggers, slowed, this long, then flips onto its back paralysed; a worker 2.5 s, a minor soldier 3, a major soldier 5 (the biggest body), king 6, queen 8. paralysed_ticks: a stung termite nobody takes lies a day, then dies (my pick; real paralysed prey lives for days, but left in the open it is eaten or dries out).
